entries.name: Nazaré (Praia do Norte)
entries.why: Big waves break here where the head of the Nazaré Canyon, a deep submarine canyon, sits close to the shore.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: EMODnet 'LIDAR DSM Nazaré' (Instituto Hidrografico, CC-BY 4.0 in metadata): 25 m grid over the coastal area; no 10 m or finer seabed grid confirmed. IH multibeam of the canyon head is mentioned in a 2012 slide deck, with no resolution or download found.

entries.name: Mavericks
entries.why: A bedrock reef off Pillar Point makes big winter swells converge and rise before breaking; typical northwest swells pass over gentler seabed.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: USGS California State Waters Map Series, Offshore of Half Moon Bay: multibeam bathymetry merged to a 2 m grid, mapped 2006-2007, from about the 10 m isobath outward; public, no licence stated, not for navigation. Shallower than 10 m may be missing.

entries.name: Teahupo'o
entries.why: A powerful reef-pass wave on the southeast coast of Tahiti; the reef shape defines where it breaks.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: Shom 'MNT topo-bathymetrique cotier de Tahiti': about 20 m (0.0002 deg), lagoons to the 100 m isobath, Licence Ouverte 2.0, updated Dec 2023; extent over Teahupo'o not confirmed. Shom Tahiti-Moorea facade DTM is about 100 m. No 10 m product found.

entries.name: Cloudbreak
entries.why: A left-hand wave breaking over coral reef about a mile or two off Tavarua island, in the Mamanuca group.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: Pacific Community (SPC) Digital Earth Pacific satellite-derived bathymetry, Sentinel-2, 10 m, CC BY 4.0, to about 30 m depth in clear water; coverage of Cloudbreak not confirmed. SOPAC Mamanuca chart (50 m) is restricted. Regional Fiji grid is about 300 m.

entries.name: Jaws (Pe'ahi)
entries.why: A big-wave break off Pe'ahi on Maui's north shore, a few miles east of Paia, where reef and offshore seabed shape the swell.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: NOAA NCEI Hawaii CUDEM 1/9 arc-second (about 3 m) bathymetric-topographic tiles, published 2021, no licence named, not subject to US copyright, not for navigation; bathymetric accuracy variable. Extent covers the main islands; Jaws tile not individually checked.

entries.name: Skeleton Bay
entries.why: A long left-hand wave over a sand bank at Donkey Bay on the Pelican Point spit, described as lasting up to about 2 km.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: none found. Coordinates are the OpenStreetMap node "Donkey Bay" (fishing spot), a point near the break, not the exact take-off; namibweb names Skeleton Bay as Donkey Bay. surf-forecast.com lists -25.92, 14.90, which looks wrong and was dropped.

entries.name: Supertubes (Jeffreys Bay)
entries.why: A long right-hand point wave at Jeffreys Bay, mapped in OpenStreetMap as a surfing spot.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: none found

entries.name: Cortes Bank (Bishop Rock)
entries.why: A seamount about 100 miles offshore whose shallowest point, Bishop Rock, lies a few feet below the surface and focuses swell.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: NCEI Coastal Relief Model Southern California V2 (2013): 1 and 3 arc-second only (about 30 m or coarser); NOAA survey H04549 exists, resolution not stated. No 10 m grid confirmed. Coordinates are the bank, not Bishop Rock itself.

entries.name: Mundaka
entries.why: A left-hand wave at the mouth of the Urdaibai estuary, where sand movement at the estuary mouth shapes the break.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: none found

entries.name: Puerto Escondido (Zicatela)
entries.why: A heavy beach-break barrel on Oaxaca's coast; submarine canyons offshore and shifting sand shape it.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: none found

entries.name: Uluwatu
entries.why: A set of reef breaks below a limestone cliff on Bali's Bukit Peninsula, where reef shape and tide control which section works.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: BIG national bathymetry BATNAS: 6 arc-second (about 180 m) and reported unreliable nearshore; no 10 m open data found. Digital Earth Pacific 10 m coverage of Bali not confirmed.

entries.name: Bells Beach
entries.why: A right-hand reef point break near Torquay on Victoria's coast, with a long surfing history.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: Victoria DEECA Victorian Coastal Digital Elevation Model 2021 (VCDEM): 10 m, CC BY 4.0; high-resolution version may have gaps, offshore extent not confirmed. A 250 cm VCDEM version also exists (CC BY 4.0).

entries.name: Duck, USACE Field Research Facility
entries.why: Surveys of shore-perpendicular profile lines around the Duck research pier have been repeated since 1979, with a public archive.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: FRF profile surveys 1979-2018 (28 lines roughly 45 m apart, ~600 m either side of pier), CC-BY-4.0 on PANGAEA, but line data not a grid. NOAA/USACE NCMP 2015 topobathy lidar (LAS point cloud) listed on InPort; resolution not stated on the record. Official FRF site unreachable this session.

entries.name: Scripps Canyon, La Jolla
entries.why: A narrow submarine canyon about 1.6 km long and 490 m deep off La Jolla, first sounded in 1937.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: USGS SIM 3324 (Scripps 2013 multibeam, Inner Continental Borderland) is public but down-sampled to 25 m, too coarse for the break. CSUMB mapped the canyon head by multibeam in October 2001 (resolution not stated); that survey is available on request from CSUMB, not as a download.

entries.name: Monterey Canyon (Moss Landing)
entries.why: Largest submarine canyon on the North American west coast, starting near Moss Landing, where Moss Landing Marine Laboratories sit.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer, for the shallow canyon head
entries.known_data: MBARI AUV 1 m grids (MGDS, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0) exist but only for 200-500 m and 1350-1880 m depths, not the nearshore. Ship multibeam 1998 raw files at NOAA NGDC; Stanford compilation is affiliates-only. Coordinates are the marine lab, canyon head is just offshore.

entries.name: Narrabeen-Collaroy, Sydney
entries.why: Monthly beach profile surveys at five sites along a 3.6 km beach have run since April 1976, with open access.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: Open profile data (CC-BY 4.0 paper, live repository at narrabeen.wrl.unsw.edu.au): five transects to 20 m depth, plus airborne lidar since 2011. A gridded open seabed product at 10 m or finer not confirmed. data.gov.au licence listings inconsistent.

entries.name: Truc Vert, Aquitaine coast
entries.why: A remote, never-nourished high-energy sandy beach with 16 years of topographic surveys published as open data.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: Shom/IGN Litto3D Nouvelle-Aquitaine 2020-2022: airborne lidar, 'metric resolution', to about 20 m depth, Etalab 2.0 open licence, not for navigation. Exact grid size not stated on the record. Beach survey DEMs on OSF under CC-BY 4.0.

entries.name: Egmond aan Zee
entries.why: North Sea beach town on the Dutch coast covered by Rijkswaterstaat's national seabed grid.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer (national grid is 20 m)
entries.known_data: Rijkswaterstaat Bathymetrie Nederland (coast and vaklodingen) covers it on a 20 m grid, CC0 1.0. No finer public grid for Egmond is confirmed.

entries.name: Perranporth, Cornwall
entries.why: A dissipative sandy macrotidal beach with surveys and wave forcing published for 2006 to 2021.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: A merged lidar and multibeam DEM on a 2 m grid is published with Scientific Data 2023 (McCarroll et al., CC-BY 4.0), hosted by the University of Plymouth. Environment Agency lidar is also distributed through the Plymouth Coastal Observatory. Exact coverage of the break is not yet confirmed.

entries.name: Heron Island, Great Barrier Reef
entries.why: A coral cay in the southern Great Barrier Reef with a University of Queensland research station.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: Heron Reef 1 m bathymetry from airborne hyperspectral data (CASI, July 2002), CC BY 3.0, on PANGAEA; not tide-corrected, with gaps. Geoscience Australia 2 m to 64 m multibeam (CC-BY 4.0) bounding box includes the island but actual coverage unconfirmed.

entries.name: Raglan (Manu Bay)
entries.why: Three left-hand point breaks, Manu Bay, Whale Bay and Indicators, about 8 km from Raglan township.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: LINZ national coastal DEM: 1 m tiles from lidar to about 25 m depth, CC-BY 4.0, on AWS Open Data. Coverage of the Raglan coast not confirmed. Waikato regional report has 50 m grids only.

entries.name: Kirra / Superbank, Gold Coast
entries.why: Pumping sand across the Tweed River mouth since 2001 has reshaped Kirra Point, where barrels once broke.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: none found. Tweed Sand Bypassing reports show 1997 and 2011 bathymetry only as report figures; no downloadable grid located.

entries.name: Funafuti Atoll
entries.why: Low-lying atoll (average elevation about two metres) whose 275 km2 lagoon and reef edge control wave exposure and flooding.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: Not confirmed. A 2004 SOPAC survey is listed with Funafuti lagoon bathymetry charts at 1:20,000 to 1:50,000 on the Pacific Data Hub, marked open, and a 2019 UNDP-supported national lidar and bathymetry survey exists but its public release is unconfirmed. A chart scale is not a grid resolution.

entries.name: Hulhumale
entries.why: Artificial island of 65,714 people (2022 census) built by pumping sand from the sea floor beside Male, a case study in reclaimed-coast exposure.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: None confirmed. A 2021 Maldives-wide gridded bathymetry paper exists (doi 10.1029/2020EA001207); its resolution near Malé and its licence are unconfirmed.

entries.name: Happisburgh
entries.why: Soft glacial-till cliffs here retreated about 20 m in 2004-2007, so processes that take millennia elsewhere are observable within a human lifetime.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer (check nearshore coverage off Norfolk)
entries.known_data: Environment Agency SurfZone DEM 2 m (LIDAR plus nearshore multibeam from the Regional Coastal Monitoring Programmes, Open Government Licence, covers lat 50-55.8N); whether it holds bathymetry off Happisburgh is unverified. EA LIDAR Composite DTM 1 m is land only.

entries.name: Grand Isle
entries.why: Barrier island at the mouth of Barataria Bay whose shoreline and wetlands buffer inland parishes from hurricane surge and waves.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: NOAA NCEI Southern Louisiana 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m) NAVD88 Coastal DEM, bbox N29.7 S28.6 E-89.8 W-91.6, not subject to US copyright, not for navigation. NCEI CUDEM 1/9 arc-second (about 3 m) tiles also exist for the contiguous US bbox (Grand Isle coverage not confirmed per tile).

entries.name: Sendai Bay
entries.why: Bay on the Miyagi coast, within the Tohoku region covered by Japan's open tsunami terrain model used for inundation calculations.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: none found at 10 m or finer. NIED Global tsunami Terrain Model whole-Japan grid is two arc-second (about 50 m), CC BY 4.0, with 2016 Cabinet Office nesting data in the Japan Trench area; Sendai Bay coverage not explicitly stated. Japan Hydrographic Association fine grids appear sold, terms unconfirmed.

entries.name: Banda Aceh coast
entries.why: Closest major city to the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake, about 249 km away, and a subject of long-term tsunami and coastal-recovery science.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: None found at 10 m or finer. Indonesia's national bathymetry (BIG, BATNAS) is listed at 6 arc-seconds (about 180 m), and public download is not confirmed; the national bathymetry system is reported as restricted to government institutions.

entries.name: Hilo Bay
entries.why: Bay on the east coast of Hawaii island with a 1908-1929 breakwater and a documented history of tsunami inundation in 1946 and 1960.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: NOAA NCEI Hilo, Hawaii 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m) integrated bathymetric-topographic DEM, built for tsunami forecasting, CC0 1.0 per its catalogue record. The record's details are inconsistent (location box and access level), so access is not yet confirmed.

entries.name: Venice Lagoon inlets (Lido)
entries.why: Tidal inlets and channels of the lagoon were mapped in 2013 before the MOSE flood barriers became operational, giving a before-baseline.
entries.needs: seabed: already available; next tier is swell model
entries.known_data: EMODnet 'Venice Lagoon Channels DTM 5 m' (CNR-ISMAR, 2013 multibeam, CC BY 4.0, not for navigation). Source paper reports 0.5 m bathymetry on MGDS (dataset licence not stated in the text).

entries.name: Cox's Bazar beach
entries.why: Long natural sea beach on a floodplain lower than the dunes, so cyclone surge and waves drive flood risk for about 196,000 residents.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: None found. A Cox's Bazar storm-surge study used bathymetry from local agencies that is not public.

entries.name: Drew Point
entries.why: Permafrost bluff coast where USGS cites erosion of up to 20 m per year, tied to storm-driven niche cutting.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: None found for Drew Point. USGS has flown airborne lidar of the north coast (topography; release not named). A 2022 USGS single-beam nearshore survey exists at Point Barrow, about 100 km west.

entries.name: Galveston Island
entries.why: Gulf barrier island protected since 1900 by a seawall and raised grade after a hurricane surge flooded the island.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: NOAA NCEI Galveston, Texas Coastal DEM, grid 1/3 arc-second (about 10 m) to 3 arc-second, MHW, bbox W-95.25 E-94.3 S28.85 N29.8, CC0 1.0 per catalogue; published 2007, so may be dated. CUDEM 1/9 arc-second (about 3 m) tiles also cover the contiguous US bbox.

entries.name: Victoria Island, Lagos
entries.why: The Eko Atlantic development next to it is built on reclaimed land lost to coastal erosion on a wave-dominated barrier coast.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: None found. A local 1 m topo-bathymetric survey at Maiyegun Estate is listed in a catalogue; its access terms are unknown. GEBCO (about 450 m) is too coarse.

entries.name: Majuro Atoll
entries.why: Atoll of 23,156 people whose highest point is under 3 m, where reef, lagoon and wave exposure shape island flooding.
entries.needs: seabed: bathymetry at about 10 m or finer
entries.known_data: Listed but not yet confirmed: a USGS 1 m topobathymetric DEM of Majuro Atoll (DOI 10.5066/F7416VXX, 1944-2016 data, satellite-derived nearshore bathymetry, RMSE about 1.1 m) and an SPC/GEM 5 m Majuro lagoon bathymetry DEM. Licences not confirmed.

notes: Coordinates marked confidence low rest on a single mapping source (OSM node or surf-forecast.com) that can differ by km between sources; verify before display. Several 'sources' URLs are the nearest article, not a page on the break itself. Wikipedia and Nominatim were rate-limited during research.

Known_data resolutions are as stated by each source and several rest on search listings only; treat any 'about 10 m or finer' claim as a lead to confirm when a contributor submits the link, not as confirmed coverage of the exact break.
Mavericks lies in the Monterey Bay / Greater Farallones sanctuary region; the mapping was announced by California OPC and NOAA Sanctuary program (sanctuarysimon.org).
Uluwatu: the cliff-top temple Pura Luhur Uluwatu charges an entry fee (reported IDR 30,000) and surf access is via a cave stairway; treat as a religious site, not verified beyond listings.
Puerto Escondido: Stab Mag reports a local sand and jetty dispute and community fundraising (Save the Waves) for bathymetric studies of Zicatela; a local-led study may be the source of future data.
Skeleton Bay: search sources disagree on access (long drive, boat, a no-4x4 local policy); whether any restricted zone applies was not confirmed.
Teahupo'o and Pe'ahi: no access or cultural restrictions were verified; check with local communities before any published directions.

Coordinates for Cloudbreak, Skeleton Bay, Teahupo'o, Puerto Escondido, Uluwatu and Jaws partly rely on surf-forecast.com or Wikipedia values that differ by km between sources; verify before display. Mavericks and Supertubes come from OSM nodes; Nazare and Bells from Wikipedia/OSM.

Wikipedia and Nominatim were rate-limited during research; pages for Cloudbreak, Jaws and Skeleton Bay were not found as dedicated Wikipedia articles (404), so some cited URLs are the closest article (Tavarua, Pe'ahi) rather than the break.
Raglan: Manu Bay's traditional name is Waikeri and the town's Maori name Whaingaroa; ancestral land taken in 1941 for an airfield, council voted 2022 to begin returning it. Use Maori names with care.
Kirra: name believed Indigenous, language and meaning unknown (Wikipedia).
Monterey MBARI grids are CC BY-NC-SA, so non-commercial use only. Scripps/CSUMB data: for-profit use needs permission.
Heron Island: resort and research station are private/institutional; island is part national park, so access is controlled.
Truc Vert is remote, over 3 km from the first car park.
Raw sources not opened (blocked): official FRF site, USGS SIM3324 data page, LINZ access page, Plymouth PEARL, Nature/Springer pages (used PMC/doi mirrors).

Banda Aceh: 2004 tsunami site with mass graves at Ulee Lheue, the Aceh Tsunami Museum and PLTD Apung 1 memorial vessel; present as a science and recovery place, not a spectacle; casualty figures conflict across sources so give none.
Hilo Bay: 1946 and 1960 tsunami deaths (165-173 and 61); avoid the 'tsunami capital' tagline.
Sendai Bay / Tohoku: 2011 tsunami memorial coast; present respectfully and do not offer surf or wave-riding framing.
Galveston: 1900 hurricane killed at least 6,000 people; keep wording factual.
Grand Isle: Hurricane Ida 2021 damaged all structures; residents still rebuilding, avoid presenting as a target.

Funafuti, Majuro, Hulhumale: living communities on climate-exposed islands; Pacific and Maldivian data may carry local data-governance expectations (SPC, UNDP, Tuvalu Lands and Survey); do not frame as doomed.
Cox's Bazar: area hosts large Rohingya refugee camps nearby; avoid presenting camp locations.
Drew Point: Alaska North Slope Indigenous lands (Inupiat); erosion affects subsistence and communities.
Lagos / Eko Atlantic: private reclamation development; Nigerian survey data may have access restrictions.
Japan JHA and JAMSTEC bathymetry carry redistribution conditions under the hydrographic law; check terms before accepting submitted links.
